accuracy.evidence: Checked against CCSS 3.MD.C.7c (tiling a rectangle with sides a and b + c shows its area is a × b + a × c), 3.OA.B.5 (distributive property, e.g. 8 × 7 = 8 × 5 + 8 × 2), the Common Core Progressions for Geometric Measurement (area models as the route to the distributive property) and the National Curriculum in England Year 3-4 multiplication guidance on partitioning. Every number recomputed: 3 × 6 = 18 = 12 + 6 for every cut 1 to 5; 6 × 13 = 60 + 18 = 78 and 6 × 10 + 3 = 63 is 15 short; 5 × (7 + 3) = 35 + 15 = 50; 4 × (6 + 2) = 24 + 8 = 32; 3 × (8 + 4) = 24 + 12 = 36; 7 × 12 = 84; 8 × 14 = 112; 6 × 15 = 90.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips for partitioned multiplication: multiplying only the first part (prediction 3 option '3', the Try 6 × 10 + 3 button showing 15 missing tiles, challenge tag 'one', p2 and m3 distractors), adding sides for area (prediction 1 option 9, 'add', m9), confusing area with perimeter ('perim'), believing a cut loses area (prediction 2, 'lose', p4), multiplying the parts together ('times', m4) and taking a number inside the brackets as the shared side (prediction 4, 'share', p5).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagdistrib is built around one mechanism, a cut line through a tiled rectangle: columns of tiles are laid over 3 by 6, a dashed cut is dragged between columns with both part areas and their sum shown live, a log of cuts writes 3 × 6 = 3 × 1 + 3 × 5 = 3 × 2 + 3 × 4, a 6 by 13 model is cut at ten, and bracket equations are built by setting the shared height and two widths. flagtiles covers area by tiling and doubling sides, flagcover what area is; neither has a cut or brackets. lab_distinct gate passes under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner finds the rule before it is stated: laying columns shows 3, 6, ... 18 tiles; every cut position keeps the green total at 18 while the two part sums change; the cut log builds the chain of equal sums; the 6 × 13 slip button shows the orange part really has 18 tiles; Check in the build step says which side is wrong (shared height or widths) rather than just 'no'.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 9 because 3 + 6 (the tiles reach 18), 'less than 18' after cutting (the total stays 18 for every cut), '6 × 10 + 3' style answer 3 (the orange part shows 6 rows of 3), and 7 or 3 as the shared side in 5 × (7 + 3) (the built model is 5 tall).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with seven distinct feedback messages that name the slip: adding sides, perimeter instead of area, a cut losing tiles, not multiplying the small part, multiplying the parts together, and using the wrong shared side. Answer order rotates so the right one is not always first.

readability.evidence: Kid explanation uses short sentences and one running example (3 by 6, then 6 × 13), with the words area, rows, part and brackets each explained in context; adult text names CCSS 3.MD.C.7c and 3.OA.B.5 and the key terms area model, partition and distributive property. validate_lessons readability passes (kid within 6.5, adult within 9.5).

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate clean. Each kid paragraph adds one idea (area as rows × columns, cutting keeps area, the bracket form, splitting at ten). Items vary the context and direction: a garden lawn and patio (m5), a missing part width (m6), choosing the easiest split (m7), reversing to find the combined width (m2) and diagnosing Mia's and Tom's errors (m3, m9).

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 light and 360 px Android dark screenshots of every step after Show me finished. The first pass had the top width label touching the heading chip, so the rectangle now starts lower; the 13-column model, the cut knob, part sums and buttons all fit with no clipping, and part labels switch to light tints in dark theme so they stay readable.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag has a labelled button twin: Lay a column and Take a column off, Cut left and Cut right, Try 6 × 10 + 3, and Height, First width, Second width minus and plus plus Check. The canvas aria-label is rewritten with every result (tiles so far, both part areas and the total, why a build is wrong). walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
